rules.quote: Use shortened forms if they help the user understand quicker.
rules.specification: The page provides no operational test for quicker understanding or audience familiarity. These require an audience profile and contextual judgement.
rules.violation_condition: A shortened form impedes understanding or is unfamiliar or unintelligible to the intended audience.
when: Applies to shortened words and phrases generally.
For acronyms and initialisms, people must recognise and understand the shortened form.
rules.why: G-2 and G-4: the general intelligibility instruction and its acronym-specific formulation concern the same problem, so they are consolidated.

rules.specification: ‘Them’ refers to contractions. The page does not define the boundary between formal and informal content.
rules.violation_condition: A contraction appears in formal content.
when: Applies when the content is formal.
rules.why: This is a distinct text property: contractions in formal content, rather than shortened forms that impede understanding.

covers.quote: People will prefer the English equivalent unless the context requires special use.

rules.quote: Use English rather than Latin shortened forms, except in some cases.
rules.specification: The page does not identify the exceptional cases or specify which contexts require special use of Latin shortened forms.
rules.violation_condition: A Latin shortened form is used instead of its English equivalent where the context does not require the Latin form.
when: The preference does not apply when the context requires special use of the Latin shortened form.
rules.why: G-2 and G-3: the contextual exception limits one preference rule; it is not a separate rule.
